correctness.rationale: For odd n and fixed 0<phi<1, remote reversal K>= (n+1)/2 has K~Bin(n,p), p=phi^2(2+phi)/[(1+phi)(1+phi+phi^2)]<1/2. The tilted law Q makes C>A balanced while both adjacent margins exceed 1/2 by delta=(1-phi^2)/(2(1+2phi)(2+phi))>0, allowing Hoeffding exponential suppression of adjacent failures on the remote event. Opposite orientation has Chernoff base beta_2 strictly less than beta by exact (1-t)^2(1+t^2)>0 at t=sqrt(phi). Stirling plus a geometric upper-tail summation yields sqrt(2/(pi n))*sqrt(p(1-p))/(1-2p)*beta^n[1+O_phi(1/n)]. Independently enumerated all 6^3 labeled ballots at phi=1/2, finding 32/1029 cycle probability, matching the package. Finite n does not prove asymptotics.
residual_risks: Excludes even electorates, correlated voters, phi=0 and the phi->1 moving-parameter boundary; tilt gap vanishes as phi->1.

evidence: Caizergues et al Section 4.2 Theorem 2 studies the last-ranked candidate winning all pairwise matches with an n^-1 two-coordinate rare tail, whereas the cycle here is one remote reversal with n^-1/2. Their Section 9 expressly proposes majority transitivity as future work. Lackner & Lackner study single-peakedness, a stronger ballot-level property with different event.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General independent preference large-deviation framework may provide methods, but no examined theorem mathematically implies the specified cycle-equivalent and orientation ratio.

evidence: Condorcet winner of last candidate requires two simultaneous rare pair reversals, not equivalent to Condorcet cycle (one remote reversal while adjacent comparisons remain normal). A single-peaked ballot culture constraint does not give the odd-electorate Mallows cycle asymptotic.

value.rationale: Majority-cycle probability is a natural social-choice invariant; the explicit sharp constant and separate exponentially suppressed orientation strengthen mere convergence-to-zero for a fixed nonuniform Mallows culture.
